newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar ends stormy week sailing calmly.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar ends stormy week sailing calmly.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar finished a torrid week on Friday in settled waters.
It closed at 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) at US$0.6773/80, having traded a mild 0.6767-80 range in the session. The Trade-Weighted Index finished at 66.29 from its 66.27 opening.
Dealers said a domestic seller, active in the market both on Thursday and Friday, was met by good demand from a variety of sources.
A sharp rise in New Zealand cash rates could see investors flocking back to the kiwi and keep it underpinned, dealers said.
"I would suggest the rates will attract into New Zealand again. It should be good for the currency in the longer run," said a Wellington bank trader.
There was little hangover from Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash's warning to markets on Thursday that conditions were too easy.
The Monetary Conditions Index remained 13 points too loose at 762 and showed few signs of backing up.
Next week the kiwi is seen pegged into a 0.6740-0.6850 range.
